messages:
maria: Hey runtime folks — noticed ~15% tail latency regression when we increase batch_size from 4 -> 8 on the A100 pool. Can someone capture an nsys + torch.profiler run (full nvtx + CUDA kernels + CPU sampling) so we can compare flamegraphs?

kevin: Which model + commit? also which input payload / batch shape?

maria: Model: redwood/llama-13b-quant (canary build), commit: 9f4b2a7. Use the eval prompt set that lives in s3://redwood-profiling/evalsets/langchain/small.json and run batch_size=4 and batch_size=8, sequence_len=1024.

ash: I can run this on rt-a100-05 today. Can you paste exact commands you want? small traces only pls.

maria: thx! Prefer the following:

```
# nsys capture
nsys profile -o /tmp/maria_batch8 -f true --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --capture-range=nvtx --capture-range-ctrl=thread --sample=cpu python serve_probe.py --model redwood/llama-13b-quant --batch 8 --seq 1024

# inside python, enable torch.profiler
with torch.profiler.profile(
    activities=[torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity.CPU, torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity.CUDA],
    schedule=torch.profiler.schedule(wait=1, warmup=1, active=3),
    on_trace_ready=torch.profiler.tensorboard_trace_handler('/tmp/torchprof_maria')
):
    run_inference_loop()
```

Please redact prompt texts before uploading. Also capture a matching run for batch 4 for baseline. Use --sample=cpu to limit size.

kevin: For nvtx capture-range, make sure the app emits NVTX spans around the top-level call (we recently added rv_infer start/stop). If not, use --capture-range=none to get whole-process.

tim: Small note — torch.profiler outputs can be huge. If you can, use schedule with small active window and run ~3 iterations per config. Also disable verbose logging and strip environment variables with secrets.

ash: ok starting capture on rt-a100-05, will upload to s3 when done. estimated 25-30 min.

tracebot: artifact upload created: s3://redwood-profiling/artifacts/2098765432/maria_batch8_nsys.tar.gz (presigned link expires in 7d)

maria: awesome, when you upload can you also paste the flamegraph conversion command? i want svg.

tim: after nsys -> nsight trace, convert to chrome trace then to flamegraph:
```
nsys export --output=/tmp/maria_batch8.json /tmp/maria_batch8.qdrep --format=json
# then use speedscope/flamegraph toolchain (internal script):
/tools/convert_trace_to_flame.sh /tmp/maria_batch8.json > /tmp/maria_batch8.svg
```
Also run `python -m torch.utils.bottleneck` if you want a quick CPU summary.

ash: uploaded both /tmp artifacts and torchprof dir to s3://redwood-profiling/artifacts/2098765432/ — kept raw names but removed prompt files. pinging here when postprocess finishes. :thumbsup:

kevin: great, i'll take a first pass at diffing flamegraphs once the svg is ready — looking for increased CPU spans or kernel shifts.

maria: thanks everyone. if you see large KV cache misses in the trace, flag me and i'll add a small reproducer.

ash: postprocess done, links:
- nsys qdrep: s3://redwood-profiling/artifacts/2098765432/maria_batch8.qdrep
- torchprof tb dir (zipped): s3://redwood-profiling/artifacts/2098765432/torchprof_maria.zip
- flame svg: s3://redwood-profiling/artifacts/2098765432/maria_batch8.svg

maria: confirmed downloads, will run diff now and post notes. thanks y'all.
